description: The Hill letter dated 12th January provides the following information regarding the origin of this violin— “The history of the Stradivari violin dated 1733, which for many years belonged to Mr. Kreisler, is as far as it is known to us as follows:— It was first seen by the late Mr. Alfred Hill in 1910 in the possession of Monsieur Gherault, an organist who lived at Rouen, who stated that he had inherited this violin from his uncle and that it had been owned by his family for nearly a century. He declined an offer made for the violin and kept it until his death in 1912, when the violin passed into the hands of his niece, Madame Demange, from whom Mr. Hill bought it in 1913. Owing to this violin having a rather exceptional quality of tone it was offered to Kreisler, who readily purchased it. At this time the violin did not possess an original Stradivari head, but Mr. Hill acquired one a few years afterwards which he fitted to the instrument. Enquiries made subsequently revealed that this violin had belonged to an amateur by the name of Uthoff in the early part of the last century. Kreisler retained this violin until 1936, when he acquired another example by the same maker. He had used this instrument when making his most famous records. It was sold shortly afterwards to Mr. Bronislaw Hubermann who retained this violin until his death.” The violin which Kreisler purchased in 1936 was the The Lord Amherst of Hackney Stradivari dated 1734 which was sold in these Rooms on 11th May 1972 (See Colour Plate)
